subject.title: Phase 2d + 2e: Data box and edits in the viewer
subject.intent: Explain the implementation plan before building it: how a click becomes a Data box, and how an edit becomes a draft, a saved diagram and a request for the agent
subject.scope: logic-builder: core, CLI server, viewer and skill

nodes.label: Click a block
nodes.desc: The user clicks a block, a state or a group on the canvas.

nodes.label: Edit a field
nodes.desc: The user clicks a pencil in the side panel and changes a name, a type, a field, a trigger or a note.

nodes.label: Agent picks up a request
nodes.desc: The user pastes the Copy-for-agent text in the chat, or just says they edited the diagram.

nodes.label: Doc on screen
nodes.desc: What the viewer shows: the diagram, or the draft while one exists, plus its issues. React state in useDocument; refetched from the server on reload.
nodes.store: React state in useDocument · lost on reload, refetched from the server
nodes.changeNote: Holds the draft's doc and the original copy while a draft exists

nodes.label: Diagram file
nodes.desc: logic/<subject>.logic.json on disk. Committed to the repo; the source of truth once saved.

nodes.label: Format and validation
nodes.desc: The JSON format, its schema and the integrity checks (Tasks 1 and 5).

nodes.label: Schema check
nodes.desc: Checks the shape of a diagram against the JSON Schema.
logic: Accepts the new fields: state.store, typeInfo, note on nodes and wires, before.source and before.context.
Rejects anything else, as today (additionalProperties: false).
nodes.changeNote: Schema gains store, typeInfo, note and the trigger before-fields

before.desc: Checks the shape of a diagram against the JSON Schema (phase 2c fields).

nodes.label: Integrity checks
nodes.desc: Reference and consistency checks the schema cannot express.
logic: Error: a typeInfo name that is not in types (unknown-type-info).
Notice: a state without store (missing-store).
Notice: a new state holding the same type as an existing one (similar-store), to push reuse before creating.
nodes.changeNote: Three new checks: unknown-type-info, missing-store, similar-store

before.desc: Reference and consistency checks (ids, ports, pins, risks, types).

nodes.label: Draft and review file names
nodes.desc: Names the side files of a diagram: booking.logic.json → booking.draft.json and booking.review.json.
logic: Strip .logic.json and add .draft.json or .review.json.
Neither ends in .logic.json, so they never show up as diagrams in the structure panel or in links.

nodes.label: Data box (phase 2d)
nodes.desc: Shows what a block reads and writes and where each piece of data lives, collapsed by default (Tasks 2 and 3).

nodes.label: Side panel
nodes.desc: The panel that opens on click. The Data box replaces its Inputs and Outputs lists.
logic: Show the explanation (what it does, how it works).
Mount the Data box, collapsed, between the explanation and the code reference.
Then code, what changes, instances and risks, as today.
nodes.changeNote: Data box replaces the Inputs / Outputs lists and the state's Holds section

before.desc: The panel that opens on click, with port lists for inputs and outputs.

nodes.label: What was clicked?
nodes.desc: Picks which kind of Data box to build.
logic: A state → who reads it and who writes it.
A group → only the data that crosses its edge.
Anything else (function, trigger, instance…) → its reads, writes and responses.

nodes.label: Reads, writes, responses
nodes.desc: One row per input (reads) and per output (writes); outputs named 200, 422… go to Responses.
logic: Each row gets where it lives: the state's store if a state feeds it, else 'from A' / 'to B'.
Each row gets up to two lines of description: the state's desc, else typeInfo.desc.
Instances use their blockType's ports.

nodes.label: Read by, written by
nodes.desc: For a state: the blocks on its read and write wires, in flow order, each clickable.
logic: Collect the blocks on read wires and on write wires.
Keep the file's wire order (story order), without duplicates.
Answers 'who already uses this store?' before a new one is created.

nodes.label: Data crossing the edge
nodes.desc: For a group: only the wires with one end inside and one outside, plus how many blocks are inside.
logic: Wires coming in are reads, wires going out are writes.
What happens inside is not listed; a muted '+N more inside' line says there is more.

nodes.label: Data box
nodes.desc: The tinted box in the panel: header 'Data · Reads 3 · Writes 2', then collapsed sections and rows.
logic: Everything starts collapsed and nothing is remembered between clicks.
Each row: name, type, where-badge, two-line description.
Opening a row asks for the type's fields and shows them as a table, with a link to the code.

nodes.label: Field table
nodes.desc: Turns a type into its fields, following names, optionals and lists.
logic: Resolve a named type through types, unwrapping T? and T[].
Return the object's fields, nested up to four levels.
Stop on recursive types instead of looping.

nodes.label: Editing (phase 2e)
nodes.desc: Small edits in the panel, applied with Design marks, kept in a draft, and turned into text for the agent (Tasks 6–8 and 10–12).

nodes.label: Input editable fields
nodes.desc: Pencil-on-hover inputs and the field table editor in the side panel.
logic: Click the pencil, type, Enter commits and Esc cancels.
On an instance, a port edit first asks 'Changes all N uses of <Type>'.
A rejected edit keeps the input open and shows the reason under it.
No pencils in the Before view, on removed items or on pins.

nodes.label: useDocument.edit()
nodes.desc: Takes an edit from the panel and hands it, with the doc on screen and the original copy, to applyEdit.
logic: On the first edit, the doc on screen becomes the original copy.
Pass the doc, the edit and the original to applyEdit.

nodes.label: applyEdit()
nodes.desc: Applies one edit to a copy of the doc and marks it the Design way, so Before/After shows what the user touched.
logic: An existing item becomes modified and keeps its first value in before; setting it back clears the mark.
A new item changes in place; removing it deletes it. Removing an existing item marks it removed, with its wires (and its children for a group).
Renaming a port rewrites its wires and keeps their old ends in before. On an instance it renames the blockType, its pin and every instance's wires.
Any edit except a note switches the file to design. A note never marks anything.
Restore copies the marks back from the original.

nodes.label: Accepted?
nodes.desc: An edit can be refused with a readable reason: empty label, duplicate port name, unparseable type, editing a removed block.
logic: Accepted → the new doc goes on screen and to the draft file.
Refused → the reason goes back to the field.

nodes.label: Click Save Button
nodes.desc: The user clicks Save in the edit bar to save the changes into the json.

nodes.label: Edit bar
nodes.desc: The bar at the bottom: 'N unsaved changes · Save · Discard', and after saving 'Saved · Copy for agent'.
logic: N counts the user's edits (a diff of draft against original).
Save is disabled while the draft has errors; the first error is shown.
If the diagram changed on disk, it warns that saving keeps the user's version and keeps the other for review.
After saving, it offers Copy for agent and names the review file if one was made.

nodes.label: summarizeEdits()
nodes.desc: Builds the Copy-for-agent request: 'I edited <file> in the viewer. Please review and implement:' plus one line per change.
logic: Diff the draft against the original copy, not the marks, so only the user's edits are listed.
One line per rename, port change, field change, trigger change, removal and note.

nodes.label: Copy IconButton for reference
nodes.desc: The copy icon on a block or wire panel, or 'Copy for agent' with several blocks selected.

nodes.label: copyReference()
nodes.desc: A reference, not the JSON: the file path, then one line per block or wire with its title, id, kind and code.
logic: First line: the diagram's path, since a subject can span several linked files.
Block: '"Title" (id: x, function) → file · symbol'.
Wire: 'wire w3: a.out → b.in (Type)'.

nodes.label: Draft server
nodes.desc: The local server behind the viewer: keeps the draft next to the diagram and saves it (Task 9).

nodes.label: PUT /api/draft
nodes.desc: Writes the draft file after each edit (debounced 300 ms in the viewer).
logic: On the first write, read the diagram's text as the original copy.
Later writes keep that original and replace the doc.
Same-origin and JSON only; atomic write.

nodes.label: Draft file
nodes.desc: <subject>.draft.json next to the diagram: the edited doc plus the original text. Survives reloads; its presence tells the agent someone is editing.

nodes.label: POST /api/save
nodes.desc: Saves the draft as the diagram.
logic: Read the draft (404 if there is none).
Validate its doc; refuse with the issues if invalid.
Compare the diagram on disk with the draft's original.

nodes.label: Draft valid?
nodes.desc: A draft with errors is never written over the diagram.
logic: No errors → go on to the disk check.
Errors → 400 with the issues, shown in the edit bar.

nodes.label: Changed on disk?
nodes.desc: Did someone (usually the agent) change the diagram while the user was editing?
logic: Same text as the draft's original → just write.
Different (even invalid JSON) → keep the disk version for review first, then write. The user's version wins.

nodes.label: Keep the other version
nodes.desc: Writes the diagram's current text to <subject>.review.json so the agent's edits are not lost.
logic: Copy the disk text as is, valid or not.
Hand the draft on to be written.

nodes.label: Review copy
nodes.desc: <subject>.review.json: the version a save set aside. Lives until the agent merges it and deletes it.
nodes.store: File <subject>.review.json · until the agent merges and deletes it
nodes.changeNote: A separate file on purpose: it holds the version a save set aside, so the diagram never loses either side.

nodes.label: Write the diagram
nodes.desc: Writes the draft's doc over the diagram and deletes the draft.
logic: Format as JSON with 2-space indent, like the bundled examples.
Atomic write (temp file + rename), then delete the draft.
Reply with ok and the review file name, if any.

nodes.label: GET /api/doc
nodes.desc: What the viewer loads on open, on reload and on every change event.
logic: Read the diagram, validate it, attach its layout (as today).
If a draft exists, also return it, its original, and whether the disk changed since.
Say whether a review copy exists.
nodes.changeNote: Returns the draft (with changedOnDisk) and the review file name

before.desc: Returns the diagram, its issues and its layout.

nodes.label: Skill: the agent's side
nodes.desc: What the agent does with the new fields and with the user's edits (Tasks 4 and 13).

nodes.label: Read the user's request
nodes.desc: Turns the pasted Copy-for-agent text, or git diff on the diagram, into requests.
logic: A renamed block, port or symbol means: rename it in the code.
An added field means: add it to the model. A removal means: drop it from the design.
A note is a request; implement it, then delete the note.

nodes.label: Draft open?
nodes.desc: Before touching a diagram, the agent checks for <subject>.draft.json.
logic: A draft exists → the user has unsaved edits: don't edit the diagram, say so and wait.
No draft → go ahead.

nodes.label: Merge the review copy
nodes.desc: If a save set the agent's edits aside, re-apply what still makes sense on top of the user's version.
logic: Compare <subject>.review.json with the diagram.
Re-apply the agent's changes that don't clash with the user's.
Delete the review copy.

nodes.label: Update the diagram
nodes.desc: The agent edits the JSON, validates it and says what changed.
logic: Every state gets a store (what the code really uses).
Reuse before creating: wire new blocks to an existing store when it holds the data; a new store needs a reason.
typeInfo only for the types that matter.
Validate until it passes.
nodes.changeNote: Adds store, typeInfo and reuse-before-create to the rules

nodes.label: Data box on screen
nodes.desc: The user sees where each piece of data comes from, where it lives and its fields.

nodes.label: Text for the agent
nodes.desc: In the clipboard, ready to paste: the edit summary after a save, or a block reference.

risks.title: Port rename loses wires in the Before view
risks.detail: If a renamed port's wires only get the new name, Before (which shows the old port) has nothing to attach them to.
risks.resolution: applyEdit keeps the old end in the wire's before; Task 7 tests that Before still draws it.

risks.title: Agent's edits lost when the user saves
risks.detail: The agent may change the diagram while a draft is open (the skill rule can be missed). A plain save would overwrite it.
risks.resolution: Save compares with the draft's original and keeps the disk text in .review.json, even if it is invalid JSON (Task 9).

risks.title: An edit that breaks the file
risks.detail: A duplicate port name or an empty label would make the saved diagram invalid.
risks.resolution: applyEdit refuses them with a reason, and the server validates again before writing (Tasks 7, 9, 11).

risks.title: Reload shows the original instead of the draft
risks.detail: After a reload or a restart of open, the viewer must come back to the draft and its edit bar.
risks.resolution: GET /api/doc returns the draft when it exists (Tasks 9 and 10).

risks.title: Removing a new block leaves dangling references
risks.detail: A deleted new block may be named by a risk or by subject.focus, which would fail validation.
risks.resolution: applyEdit strips deleted ids from risk refs and drops a focus that no longer exists (Task 7).

risks.title: Local draft overwritten by a refetch
risks.detail: Each PUT triggers a change event; a refetch that lands before the next PUT could replace newer local edits.
risks.resolution: The server's draft wins only when no PUT is pending (Task 10).

risks.title: One click renames a port in every use
risks.detail: Instances share their blockType's ports, so a port edit on one instance changes all of them.
risks.resolution: The panel asks first: 'Changes all N uses of <Type>' (Task 11).
